'''Joseph Oesterlé''' (born 1954) is a French mathematician who, along with [[David Masser]], formulated the [[Abc conjecture|''abc'' conjecture]] which has been called "the most important unsolved problem in [[diophantine analysis]]".<ref>[http://www.numdam.org/numdam-bin/fitem?id=SB_1994-1995__37__333_0 Oesterlé „Travaux de Wiles II“, Seminar Bourbaki 1994/5] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303172537/http://www.numdam.org/numdam-bin/fitem?id=SB_1994-1995__37__333_0 |date=2016-03-03 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.numdam.org/numdam-bin/fitem?id=SB_1987-1988__30__165_0 Oesterlé „Nouvelles approches de Theoreme de Fermat“, Seminar Bourbaki 1987/8, abc Conjecture] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227073649/http://www.numdam.org/numdam-bin/fitem?id=SB_1987-1988__30__165_0 |date=2015-12-27 }}</ref>

He is a member of [[Nicolas Bourbaki|Bourbaki]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Maurice Mashaal|title=Bourbaki: A Secret Society of Mathematicians|publisher=AMS|year=2006|page=17|url=https://www.ams.org/bookstore-getitem/item=bourbaki}}</ref>
